sections.principal_activity: Principal activities The principal activity of the group in the period under review was that of dispensing chemists. Amiry & Gilbride Healthcare Limited is the holding company for its subsidiaries: LP North Fourteen Limited and LP North Fifteen Limited. Both subsidiaries were acquired during the period and both commenced trading from 1 August 2023.
sections.strategic_report: STRATEGIC REPORT FOR THE PERIOD ENDED 31 JULY 2024 \- 1 - The directors present the strategic report for the period ended 31 July 2024. Business overview The group was formed following the merger of two established multiple-pharmacy operators to create a new joint venture business. The group was specifically established to acquire pharmacy assets released during the divestment and break-up of one of the UK’s largest pharmacy operators. As part of this process, the group successfully acquired eleven pharmacies under its holding company and two trading legal entities. The acquisitions provided a strong platform for growth and enabled the group to establish a competitive footprint across its operating regions. Centralised operations and investment To support rapid growth and efficiency, the group invested significantly in centralised operations, securing a dedicated off-site building to house three core functions: Pick 2 Prescription Hub & Spoke Dispensing – designed to handle up to 70% of the group’s dispensing volume at hub level. PillPouch Solution – robotic pouch preparation and automated checking to replace traditional monitored dosage systems. Central Warehouse Function – consolidated procurement and redistribution of medicines across the branch network. This infrastructure investment included recruitment of new teams, creation of new processes, and initial stock purchasing to establish the hubs. Diversification of services Aligned with the group’s vision for a modern, patient-centred pharmacy model, significant investment was made in service diversification to reduce reliance on NHS income. Teams were trained and deployed to deliver: Travel clinics Children’s vaccination services Private blood testing services Diagnostic testing services Private pharmacy services Ear health clinics NHS services were also strengthened by training pharmacists as independent prescribers for Pharmacy First Plus, and supporting career development into technician and accuracy-checking roles. Technology and sustainability The group is committed to building a technology-enabled, sustainable pharmacy model. Investment during the year has included: Bespoke Patient App – prescription management, health advice, and communication. New Website with Online Booking – full digital booking system for NHS and private services. 24/7 Automated Collection Points – secure, convenient medicine access. Green Fleet Transition – new electric mopeds with a goal of full green delivery by end of 2025. Retail development Working with a leading pharmacy wholesaler, the group has redesigned its retail spaces to: Promote health, wellbeing, and self-care purchases. Modernise layouts for improved patient journeys. Strengthen commercial performance with a more relevant front-of-shop proposition. AMIRY & GILBRIDE HEALTHCARE LIMITED STRATEGIC REPORT (CONTINUED) FOR THE PERIOD ENDED 31 JULY 2024 \- 2 - Financial and sustainability Significant upfront investment in infrastructure and services has created a strong foundation for growth: The group is outperforming national market share growth in Scotland at twice the average rate. Private services revenues are increasing, reinforcing resilience beyond NHS funding. Trading has been impacted by NHS underpayments, recognised outside trading reports but expected to be recovered. In the first twelve months, performance was also affected by one-off, non-recurring items: Remittances for stock purchased by the former owner under the transitional services agreement, not disclosed until after completion. Estimated NHS payments in place of actual reconciliations for the first six months of trading. These items have been treated transparently to provide a clear picture of underlying performance. Key performance indicators (KPIs) The directors monitor performance using a range of financial and operational KPIs, including: Turnover Growth – year-on-year revenue performance monitored against budget and sector benchmarks. Gross Profit Margin – tracked monthly to assess procurement efficiency, pricing strategy, and service mix sustainability. Market Share Growth – group pharmacies are expanding at approximately twice the Scottish national average. Prescription Volume – maintained strong growth, with central hub capacity to absorb up to 70% of dispensing volume. Private Service Revenues – continued increases across travel health, diagnostics, vaccinations, and testing. Patient Access Metrics – volume of online bookings and uptake of 24/7 automated collection points. Sustainability Progress – proportion of deliveries completed via the green fleet. Staff Development – number of pharmacists trained as prescribers and staff achieving technician and accuracy-checking roles. These KPIs provide a balanced assessment of financial performance, operational efficiency, patient access, and workforce development. Risk management The group operates in a complex regulatory and commercial environment. The directors have identified the following key risks and mitigation strategies: NHS Funding Risk – ongoing underfunding and delayed payments impact cashflow. Mitigation: diversification into private services, advance payment models, and financial reserves. Supply Chain Risk – shortages and pricing volatility. Mitigation: central warehouse redistribution, bulk purchasing, and wholesaler partnerships. Regulatory Risk – evolving healthcare regulation. Mitigation: compliance teams, training, and prescriber qualifications. Technology & Cyber Risk – reliance on digital systems. Mitigation: secure IT infrastructure, audits, and data protection. Workforce Recruitment & Retention – shortage of pharmacists. Mitigation: career pathways, training investment, competitive packages.
